summary: Deployed the supplied stdio handler on node1 through xinetd TCP/9097. Sequential and concurrent protocol tests pass, no handler processes remain, protocol notes are unchanged, and persistence was verified by restarting node1 and node2 individually.
actions_performed: Installed the signed RHEL 7-compatible xinetd 2.3.15 package.
Configured a wait=no xinetd service for the supplied handler and enabled it at boot.
Opened TCP/9097 in runtime and permanent firewalld configuration.
Verified PING→PONG and all other tested lines→ERROR from node2.
Verified distinct per-connection handler processes under concurrency and complete child cleanup.
Preserved the operating-system release, kernel, handler, and protocol notes.
Restarted each node separately and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.summary: Signed xinetd package installed; wait=no service points to the supplied handler; xinetd is enabled, active, listening on 9097, and firewalld permits the port.
PING returned PONG; HELLO and an empty line returned ERROR.

Twelve held connections produced twelve distinct handler PIDs and clean exits. A final post-restart run completed 16/16 concurrent PONG requests with zero non-PONG responses and zero remaining handlers.

evidence.requirement: Protocol notes and legacy platform preserved
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64. Final handler/protocol hashes match the baseline, and protocol.txt retains its original text.
